newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends up sharply after volatile swings.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends up sharply after volatile swings.

text.p: CME lumber futures posted an extremely wide trading range of $13.00 per tbf before again rallying to close sharply higher in the nearby.

November ran up for a $8.10 per tbf gain then tumbled to a $4.90 loss before running up again to end $6.80 higher at $344.70. Other months ended $3.30 higher to unchanged with January up $3.30 at $357.70 per tbf.

Traders appeared divided on the direction of futures, especially in view of sharply falling cash lumber prices and current sharp discount of futures to cash. Trading was light at times, adding to the volatility, traders said.
"The bulls are claiming that futures are acting like they bottomed and the bears are saying its a dead cat bounce and short covering," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
Reports that interest was developing for cash lumber at recent lower levels provided some support off and on through the day, traders said.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce Wednesday at $367 per tbf, down $15 from Friday and $25 under a week ago. Cash spruce prices have fallen $65 from the recent cash high of $432 per tbf in mid-September.
